name: Rings
oneLiner: Every shape a circle: the $10,000 month as a ring meter on soft lilac.
concept:
Nonprofit Megaphone's product is a number that has to stay full every month: $10,000 of Google search ads, spent well and kept above a 5% click-through floor, or the account is at risk. Rings makes that number the brand. The hero object is a ring meter: an outer violet ring for budget spent ($9,847 of $10,000, tagged SAMPLE MONTH, with a white playhead where it stops), an inner deeper-violet ring for click-through with a black tick at Google's 5% floor, and a white disc holding the figures. Everything around it obeys the same rule. Stats sit in white circles on a dotted orbit, the certification is a badge with text running around its rim, the account lead and the CEO are circular portraits, buttons and nav are full pills, the client roll is separated by violet dots, and the only straight edges on the page belong to the page itself.

The palette is one ground, one ink, one colour: soft lilac-gray #EEEDF5, which no other direction uses, near-black #16151C, and a vivid violet #5B3DF5 with a deeper #3F2BC0 for hover and small text, plus white for every circle. Outfit's truly round letterforms carry the display and Figtree the body; there is no mono voice at all. The register is friendly, modern and precise, a product-brand feel that stays warm because the human counterweights are built in: Amber Snow's 'person, not a policy' guarantee under the CTA, a named account lead on the orbit, Michelle Hurtado's letter in the trust strip. Motion is CSS only: the rings draw on, the satellites pop into place, the badge turns slowly, and reduced-motion users get the finished meter instantly.
distinctFrom: It is the only direction built from whole closed circles as objects on a lilac ground, where Amplitude's arcs radiate from an origin on warm paper and every other direction is built from rules, cards or rectangles.
bullets: Concentric ring meter: $9,847 of $10,000, the 5% floor as a tick.
Lilac ground, one violet, white circles; no visible corners anywhere.
Stats, portraits, badge, buttons and nav are all circles or pills.
rightFor: A leadership team that wants a modern, friendly product-brand feel, one owned shape, and a monthly meter clients will actually check.
needs: Approve violet replacing the brand blue
Consent one redacted account for the meter
Fund circular portraits of the team
Build the ring meter as a component

palette.note: Soft lilac-gray for every page; unclaimed by any other direction. The 18px dot grid (ink at 16%) appears only behind the hero meter, masked to fade out 330px from the centre, and is dropped on phones.

Every white shape is a circle or a full pill: ring tracks, stat satellites, the centre disc, the nav pill, the ghost button, the eyebrow, the trust stamp, the phone's letter pill. Shadows are soft (14/30px at 28% ink with negative spread) so circles float rather than sit.
Headlines, figures, the lead pill and the 100% disc, the 5% tick, the dotted orbit, the dot grid and the dotted section rule. 15.6:1 on lilac, 18:1 on white; never pure black.
Sub copy and eyebrow text. 9.2:1 on lilac.
Labels, captions, units, the client-roll label. 5.4:1 on lilac and 6.3:1 on white, so every 11px label passes AA.

The one chromatic colour: the spend ring, the mark, primary buttons, the eyebrow and roll dots, the ring icon, the moons, and exactly one headline phrase per page. 5.3:1 on lilac and 6.1:1 under white text, so it works both as a fill and as large text; never as text under 24px.
Hover and pressed buttons, the inner click-through ring, and any violet text under 24px: the quote link, the SAMPLE tag, the badge text, 'Letter from Google'. 7.8:1 on lilac, 9.1:1 on white.
The SAMPLE and '2 min' tag fills, the eyebrow dot's halo, the phone stamp disc, and the 16% violet glow behind the meter. Muted text on it measures 4.9:1, deep violet 7.0:1.

typography.display: Outfit (Google Fonts): 700 for h1, the meter figure, satellite and ticker figures and the phone fact lines; 600 for the wordmark; 500 for the Michelle Hurtado quote. Its o, c, e and zero are near-perfect circles, which is why it carries the whole system; never used below 14px.
typography.body: Figtree (Google Fonts): 400 body, 500 nav links, units, captions and fine print, 600 buttons, labels, eyebrows and inline emphasis, 700 for the SAMPLE tag and the tracked 11px labels. Two families total, loaded from fonts.googleapis.com only; no Fontshare, no self-hosting.
typography.scaleNotes: Desktop h1 60px / .98 / -0.03em in two lines ('$10,000 a month,' / 'kept full.'), sentence case, exactly one phrase in violet. Meter figure 44px Outfit 700; satellite figures 32 and 24px; ticker figures 28px; quote 21px Outfit 500. Body 18px / 1.5 at max-width 470px; guarantee 15px; fine print 12px Figtree 500. Labels, eyebrows and tags are 11px Figtree 600-700, uppercase, 0.06-0.12em tracking; 11px is the floor and nothing is set below it. Phone: h1 38px / 1.0, meter figure 21px, facts 18px Outfit 700 over 12px Figtree 500, body 16px / 1.5, quote 16px. Buttons are pills: 56px in the desktop hero (44px nav), 52px phone primary, 48px phone secondary, 36px phone nav; time tags are 30px and 28px pills at 11px. Spacing on an 8px base: nav 80, hero 584, trust 187 on desktop (frame 851px); nav 64 on the phone. Every figure carries a unit, and the meter carries SAMPLE MONTH until a consented account replaces it.

layout:
- Grid: 12 columns, 1200px container, 48px gutters at desktop, 24px tablet, 16px phone; vertical rhythm on 8px. No section rules and no cards: sections are separated by a dotted rule (1.2px ink dots at 12px pitch) and a section number in a 32px white disc (01, 02, 03). The ring token set (orbit, spend ring, click-through ring, disc) appears at most three times per page: hero, services, reporting.
- 00 Nav (80px, no rule): violet disc mark (white ring and dot) + 'Nonprofit Megaphone' Outfit 600 with an 11px 'Google Ad Grant management' line; Services, Our work, Happy clients, Team, Blog inside one white pill, the active link a lilac pill with a violet dot; 'Get a free quote' in deep violet; 'Book a free call' violet pill whose white ring fills on hover. Past the hero the nav pill gains a soft shadow and the CTA compresses to ring + 'Book'.
- 01 Hero (584px; 560px copy column, 640px field): eyebrow pill 'One of the first nine agencies certified by Google'; h1 '$10,000 a month, / kept full.' with the phrase in violet; sub naming the $10,000 and the 5% floor; action row = violet 'Book a free call · 15 min' pill + white 'Am I eligible? · 2 min' pill with a ring-and-dot icon; fine print with violet dot separators; guarantee row with Amber Snow's circular portrait, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy' and 'Read the guarantee'. Field: an 18px dot grid fading from the centre, a violet halo, and the 460px dial: dotted orbit (36 dots), spend ring 20px (98.47% violet with a white playhead), click-through ring 13px (84% deep violet with a black tick at the 5% point), white 200px disc with SAMPLE MONTH, $9,847, 'of $10,000 spent', '8.4% click-through'; satellites at 35, 128, 220 and 305 degrees: 780+ nonprofits (124px), $48M+ managed (96px), the turning CERTIFIED BY GOOGLE · ONE OF NINE badge (108px, a link), a violet moon and an ink moon; the 'Google's 5% floor' label pill under the rings; the ink lead pill 'Your account lead · one named contact · $10,000/mo in' centred at the foot of the orbit. Reading order: disc, floor label, satellites, lead.
- 02 Trust strip (dotted rule above, 187px): white stamp disc, 'Letter from Google · Michelle Hurtado, Google's first Head of Ad Grants', the quote in 21px Outfit 500; two 104px circles, 100% (ink) 'acquisition guaranteed' and 60+ 'person team'; the client roll 'Among 780+ clients · Sep 2026' with UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, Solar Sister, AAU, JFCS separated by violet dots.
- 03 The rules (policy literacy): Google's requirements as seven circular chips arranged around one sentence ('Miss the 5% floor two months running and Google can deactivate the account'); each chip expands into a pill with requirement / what Google does if you miss it / what we do about it, covering 5% CTR, conversion tracking, single-word keywords, account structure, monthly login, geo-targeting, quality score; dated source link to Google's policy page.
- 04 Eligibility checker (rep-free exit): three questions as pill toggles (org type, country, working website) beside a small ring that fills one third per answer; a full ring offers the call; hospitals, schools and governments get an honest 'not eligible, here's why' disc quoting Google's definition.
- 05 Outcomes: twelve case files as circular tiles (wordmark, vertical, twelve-month period) with filter pills for the 12 verticals; each opens a pill card with input, outcome, period, source, 'Open case file' and 'Forward to board (PDF)'. Every figure is verified with the client before launch.
- 06 What it costs: a flat monthly fee stated in one sentence if leadership approves it, never a percentage of spend; the seven services as a row of rings each filled to its share of a typical engagement, Ad Grant management fullest (Ad Grant management, Website SEO, Content creation, VisitorEmail, Google Remarketing, Microsoft Advertising, Spanish ad creation). Second appearance of the ring token.
- 07 One of nine (contained ink band with rounded ends, not full-bleed): the inaugural Google Ad Grants Certified Professional fact, the Google Partner badge inside a white circle with its clear-space rules, Inc. 5000 x4 as circular seals.
- 08 Your team, named: circular colour portraits of six to eight people on an orbit around a 'your account lead' disc; role and 'Nonprofits I support' captions; the cabin-retreat candid cropped in one large circle; copy stating who the prospect's named contact will be.
- 09 Reporting, shown: a real monthly report rendered as the same ring meter with a named client and month, plus compliance dots (a filled violet dot is 'met', a hollow ring is 'open'; no green exists in the system); beside it the one-sentence month signed by the account lead with a circular portrait and date. Third appearance of the ring token.
- 10 Guarantee band (ink ground): the $25 CEO guarantee in 52px Outfit 700, Amber Snow's circular portrait, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy', one violet pill.
- 11 FAQ: five plain-language questions as pills that expand (why pay for something free; will it raise money, answered honestly; who is on my account; what if we get suspended; how long to acquire), each with a dated source where a policy is cited.
- 12 Final CTA row: the hero action pair repeated verbatim plus 'See a real account report' link opening a redacted PDF.
- 13 Footer: four columns, circled social icons, a pill newsletter input, address, client-login link; 780+ used consistently; print stylesheet for case files and the guarantee page.
imagery: No illustration system and no stock photography. Four image types only. First, the ring meter: inline SVG circles with pathLength=100 and stroke-dasharray, so each fill is a number in the markup ($9,847 of $10,000 = 98.47; 8.4% on a 0-10 scale = 84) and editors change the value, not the drawing; tokens are ring radius, stroke width, tick position and colour, exported per breakpoint (460px desktop, 172px phone). Second, photography of NPM's people in circular crops only: colour, eye-level, shot on a plain lilac backdrop so the crop reads as a disc rather than a hole; Amber Snow and the account lead in the hero (CSS placeholder discs with role='img' labels until the shoot), six to eight team portraits on the orbit in section 08. Third, real screens: the monthly report re-rendered as the ring meter with a named client, month and visible SAMPLE or REDACTED pills, never blur. Fourth, the client roll and badges as typography: wordmarks in Figtree 500 separated by violet dots, the certification as text on a circular path, Inc. 5000 as circular seals, so no logo licensing is needed. Iconography is a 2px stroke set built only from rings and dots (ring-and-dot for eligibility, three dots for the menu, a ring that fills for the CTA). Data viz: lilac ground, white tracks, violet series one, deep violet series two, ink ticks for thresholds, a unit and a period on every chart, and Google's 5% floor as a tick wherever click-through is charted.
motion: Static first; the finished meter is the design and nothing depends on JavaScript. 1. Hero load (pure CSS, shipped in the mockup): the spend ring draws clockwise from twelve o'clock over 1.2s, the click-through ring follows at 0.45s, the disc, satellites, moons, floor label and lead pill scale up from 86% with a 0.05-1.05s stagger, then the playhead and tick fade in at 1.25s; copy is readable from frame one. 2. The certification badge turns once every 48 seconds, slow enough to read and the only loop on the page; it can be cut to a hover-only turn if the client prefers stillness. 3. Phone: the same two rings draw and the four fact rows pop in 150ms apart. 4. Hover: the white ring inside every violet button fills solid, the ghost button's hairline turns violet and the badge gains one, nav links gain a lilac pill; pressed buttons darken to #3F2BC0. 5. Below the fold (optional GSAP + ScrollTrigger sprint, native scroll only, no Lenis, JS budget under 300kB): section rings draw at 30% in view, the services rings fill in sequence, FAQ pills expand, the ticker counts up with tabular figures and a static 'as of' date. 6. prefers-reduced-motion: every keyframe lives inside a no-preference media query, so reduced-motion users get the complete meter, a still badge and no keyframes at all. 7. Never: WebGL, kinetic type, parallax on portraits, autoplaying video, scroll-jacking, or a meter that re-animates on every scroll.
mobile: The 390px hero is its own composition, not the dial shrunk. Nav (64px): 36px violet disc, 'Nonprofit Megaphone' 14px Outfit 600, a 36px 'Book a call' pill and a 40px white circle menu button with three dots. Hero (16px gutters): 'Certified by Google · one of nine' eyebrow pill; h1 38px holding two lines ('$10,000 a month,' / 'kept full.'); then the meter as a 172px dial beside a dotted fact list: SAMPLE MONTH pill, '$9,847 spent / of the $10,000 budget', '8.4% click-through / Google's floor is 5%' with an ink dot matching the tick, '780+ nonprofits / served, $48M+ managed'; the disc holds $9,847 and 'of $10,000'. Then a four-line sub, a full-width 52px violet 'Book a free call · 15 min' pill and a full-width 48px white 'Am I eligible? · 2 min' pill (a button, not a text link), and a centred fine-print line with dot separators. The primary CTA sits at about 520px and the eligibility button at about 585px, both inside a 760px fold. One trust element follows: the Letter from Google as a white pill with a tinted stamp disc, the quote at 16px Outfit 500, and 'Letter from Google · Michelle Hurtado, first Head of Ad Grants'. Below the fold the trust circles become a horizontal row of 88px discs, the client roll wraps to two dotted lines, the rules become a vertical dotted list, outcome tiles go two-up, the services rings sit three per row at 72px, and the team orbit becomes a two-column grid of circular portraits. Tap targets are 44px minimum; the dot grid and halo are dropped; the badge does not turn on phones.
a11y: Target WCAG 2.2 AA across the system. Contrast, measured on the actual backgrounds: #16151C ink on lilac 15.6:1 and on white 18:1; #3E3D4A body on lilac 9.2:1; #5F5E70 muted labels on lilac 5.4:1 and on white 6.1:1, so 11px labels pass; #5B3DF5 violet on lilac 5.3:1 (headline phrase, dots, rings) and white on #5B3DF5 6.1:1 (buttons); #3F2BC0 deep violet on lilac 7.8:1 and on white 9.1:1 (every violet text under 24px); #C9C6DB on the ink pill and the 100% disc 10.9:1; the '15 min' tag is an outline, not a fill, so its white text sits on the button's own violet at 6.1:1; muted text on the #E4DFFC tags 4.9:1. Measured frame: desktop 851px (nav 80 + hero 584 + trust 187); phone primary CTA at about 520px and eligibility at about 585px inside a 760px fold; nothing overflows 1200px or 390px. Type floor: 11px for labels and tags, 12px fine print, 14-18px everything else; nothing is set below 11px. Meter semantics: the dial is a figure with aria-labelledby pointing to a visually hidden figcaption that states spend, click-through, the 5% tick and that the figures are sample data; the SVG rings, dots, playhead, tick, moons and grid are aria-hidden; every figure, label and satellite is real DOM text in reading order; the turning badge is a link with a full aria-label and its circular text is aria-hidden; portrait placeholders carry role='img' with descriptive labels until photographs replace them. Focus: a 2px #3F2BC0 outline with 3px offset and a 999px radius on every link and button via :focus-visible, visible on lilac, white, violet and ink. Motion: every animation is inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so reduced-motion users get the finished meter and a still badge with zero keyframes; nothing autoplays beyond the 1.4s load sequence except the 48s badge turn, which stops under reduced motion. Colour is never the only signal: the 5% floor is a tick plus a labelled pill, compliance states are filled versus hollow, and the meter states its numbers in text. Pointer targets 44px on touch; buttons 48-56px. Headings are sentence case; uppercase is reserved for 11px tracked labels.

heroCopy.eyebrow: One of the first nine agencies certified by Google
heroCopy.headline: $10,000 a month, kept full.
heroCopy.sub: Google gives eligible nonprofits $10,000 a month in search ads. We acquire it, keep it above Google's 5% click-through floor, spend it well, and send one plain monthly report your board can read in a minute.

signatureMoments: The ring meter: budget spent as an outer violet ring ($9,847 of $10,000 with a playhead where it stops), click-through as an inner ring with Google's 5% floor as a black tick, and a white disc holding the figures under a SAMPLE MONTH tag, so the first screen shows the thing clients pay to have watched.

The dotted orbit with satellites: 780+ and $48M+ in white circles, a slowly turning CERTIFIED BY GOOGLE · ONE OF NINE badge, two small moons and the named account lead on an ink pill, the proof arranged around the meter like a dial instead of stacked in a list.
The ring that fills: every violet 'Book a free call' pill carries a white ring that becomes a solid dot on hover, a two-second brand memory that survives any Webflow edit.

A page with no corners: nav, eyebrow, buttons, tags, stat tiles, portraits, stamps, the client roll's dot separators and even the section rule (a row of dots) are circles or full pills, so the site is recognisable from a blurred thumbnail.

The human counterweights: Amber Snow's circular portrait and 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy' directly under the CTA, and Michelle Hurtado's letter opening the trust strip, keeping a geometric system warm.
dependencies: Approve violet #5B3DF5 replacing the current blue as the single brand colour, and redraw the megaphone mark as a violet disc with a white ring and dot; keeping the blue mark would add a second chromatic colour and break the system.
Consent from one client for a real redacted month to replace the SAMPLE meter, or keep the SAMPLE MONTH tag permanently; the hero meter never shows unlabelled figures.

Name the account leads publicly and fund a photography half-day for circular colour portraits of Amber Snow, the leads and six to eight team members on a plain backdrop; the mockups ship with labelled placeholder discs.

Build the ring meter as a Webflow embed symbol whose fill is a single number field, plus a style-guide page that locks the two families, the pill radius and the rule that nothing gets a square corner.
Confirm the badge wording ('Certified by Google · one of nine') against the Google Ad Grants Certified Professional programme terms and the Partner badge clear-space rules.
risks: Violet and pills are the visual language of SaaS; without the human counterweights (Amber Snow under the CTA, a named lead on the orbit, circular team portraits, the signed monthly note) the site could read as a dashboard product rather than an agency of sixty people.

A meter showing 98.5% spent and 8.4% click-through sets expectations; the SAMPLE tag, the figcaption and the sub copy keep it honest, but sales must be ready for 'will mine look like that?', and the reporting section should show a real month with a real number.

Circles waste space: stat discs hold two short lines at most, the badge holds 36 characters, and long client names or a twelve-word eyebrow break the system; copy discipline and a locked class set are part of the build, not a nice-to-have.

Dropping brand blue is a bigger change than the other directions ask for; 780 existing clients will notice, and the wordmark, favicon, email templates and report PDFs all need the violet disc at the same time.
references: Apple Watch Activity rings (a live meter as identity, threshold as a mark on the ring)
Headspace (one warm colour, round type, circles and dots as a whole system without SaaS chrome)
Oura and Fitbit dashboards (concentric ring meters that people check monthly)
Lemonade (a single vivid colour, pill buttons, friendly precision on a pale ground)
Outfit and Figtree specimen pages (geometric round display over a humanist body)
